Notes: Earliest documented reference to Jews in Judenburg (medieval community)
Jew Suessman named in a document; first named Jew of Judenburg
Jewish judge recorded in Judenburg; documentary evidence of Jews begins 1290
Early 15th c. (year is approximate midpoint of stated period): 22 Jewish wholesale dealers each with fortune over 100000 gulden; organized community with Judengasse
Emperor Frederick III permitted the city to expel non-taxpaying Jews; partial expulsion
Expulsion of all Jews from Styria ordered 1496 (by 1497); Jewish settlement then prohibited until second half of 19th c. (source: no community existed until 19th c.)
16 families (42 persons) at time of Anschluss; prayer room closed and confiscated
By February 1939 all Jews had left the city mostly for Vienna; town declared judenrein spring 1939
Article of 15 June 1945: not a single Jew can be found in the town
Only three Jewish families remained in the district (district-level not town; Population blank)
Memorial with two rings: 40 names from pre-1496 community and 97 names from 1938 onward (name lists incomplete; not a population count)
